game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: henriqueslade
quote: There are many moments where, if Jason’s body bumps into destructible objects—like a boat motor—the object gets destroyed. This is a far cry from the "realism" Rockstar claimed the game would have. Then there are things like objects simply vanishing from NPCs' hands. The severity of an alligator bite makes no sense; it’s supposed to be devastating, yet it only causes a small amount of damage to the character. Crashing a motorcycle head-on into a tree doesn't even break the handlebars. Characters can "tank" gunfire—they don't take much damage at all—which completely contradicts Rockstar’s claims of "realism." NPCs don't have the freedom they promised; they just stay in the same spot for days on end. Graphically, the game isn't much of a leap from GTA V, especially considering the 13-year wait—it’s hardly a massive improvement. Many elements are just copied from its predecessor. The game is riddled with bugs—it feels like that other game that ends in "77." GTA 6 feels more like *Fast & Furious* than a *Grand Theft Auto* game. Every time Lucia appears on screen, the camera focuses on her backside—it’s completely unnecessary. This *GTA* is definitely not for kids; it’s full of pornography, drug scenes, and more—it’s not at all suitable for children or teenagers. In short, it falls well short of expectations—13 years for this? Nothing special at all.
